caption: Overview of the benchmark. Each entry e = (h, R) supplies its header and exactly the papers the curators cited, each readable as full text, abstract or title only depending on open access; the causal gene is withheld. One model writes every draft, and only the generation strategy varies: three paradigms (read and write; extract, then write; memory first), a memory-only control with no papers, and three add-ons (dashed), each tested against its parent. The same mechanical guards apply to every strategy. Every draft then passes through the same claim-level audit against the cited papers and is scored against the same reference: curator-written per-paper text (OMIM allelic-variant descriptions in ClinVar), split once into fixed fact lists for the primary endpoint, OMIM facts conveyed, and HPO disease annotations, allelic variants, causal gene and inheritance for the secondary measures. Counts are for the 100-entry main set.
description: Three-panel left-to-right schematic (7.2 x 3.1 in). Input: entry e=(h,R), header h, cited papers with access-level icons (full text, abstract, title), causal gene withheld, counts 100 entries / 515 papers (96 full text, 345 abstract, 74 title only). Strategy panel (the only variable): Read and write (Direct reading with dashed add-ons Second-hand evidence and Learned curation guide; Agentic curator), Extract, then write (Evidence graph; Case table first with dashed add-on Reconciled case database), Memory first (Recall, then verify), Control (Memory only, no papers); band of shared guards below. Right: claim-level audit (atomic claims -> verdict per cited paper + verbatim quote -> one repair round) feeding scoring (OMIM facts conveyed primary, fixed fact lists; secondary HPO terms, allelic variants, causal gene, inheritance), fed by the reference box (curator-written per-paper text (OMIM allelic-variant descriptions in ClinVar): 476 paragraphs, 6,652 fixed facts; HPO disease annotations 2,311; OMIM allelic variants in ClinVar 427; causal gene; inheritance modes). Okabe-Ito colours per paradigm.
